# DebugTools

> Open-source debugging toolkit for logs, traces, APIs, auth, CI, mobile, Kubernetes, OpenTelemetry, and production issues.

DebugTools is local-first by default. Pasted logs, tokens, stack traces, crash reports, HAR files, and build failures stay in the browser unless the user explicitly chooses a network or AI workflow.

## Start Here

- [Homepage](https://debugtools.org/): Project overview and primary tools.
- [API Workbench](https://debugtools.org/tools/api/): Browser REST client with collections, auth, environments, imports, and response inspection.
- [All tools](https://debugtools.org/tools/all/): Complete tool registry.
- [Developer answers](https://debugtools.org/answers/): Concise answer pages for common debugging workflows.
- [Roadmap](https://debugtools.org/roadmap/): Shipped and planned debugging tools.
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/jasimvkarim/mydebugtools): Source code, issues, license, and contribution workflow.

## Primary Debugging Tools

- [API Workbench](https://debugtools.org/tools/api/): Flagship REST client with collections, auth, environments, imports, and response inspection.
- [CI Debugger](https://debugtools.org/tools/ci-debugger/): Inspect GitHub Actions workflows for jobs, steps, local act commands, and risky patterns.
- [HTTP Traffic Inspector](https://debugtools.org/tools/http-profiler/): Inspect HAR exports for timing, redirects, failures, payload sizes, and slow requests.
- [Kubernetes Debug Helper](https://debugtools.org/tools/k8s-debug/): Detect common pod failure signals and generate focused kubectl debug commands.
- [Log Trace Rebuilder](https://debugtools.org/tools/log-trace/): Group multiline logs by trace ID, request ID, correlation ID, severity, and related details.
- [OpenTelemetry Trace Viewer](https://debugtools.org/tools/otel-trace-viewer/): Summarize OTLP traces, spans, root spans, error spans, and slow operations.
- [Security Headers Inspector](https://debugtools.org/tools/security-headers/): Score response headers, missing browser protections, and cookie security flags.
- [Stack Trace Explainer](https://debugtools.org/tools/stack-trace/): Extract error type, root frame, app frames, dependencies, and likely cause from pasted stack traces.

## Answer Pages

- [What is the best free JSON formatter for developers?](https://debugtools.org/answers/best-free-json-formatter/): The best free JSON formatter validates syntax, formats nested payloads clearly, and keeps sensitive JSON local to your browser when possible.
- [How do I decode a JWT safely?](https://debugtools.org/answers/how-to-decode-jwt-safely/): Decode JWTs in a local browser tool, review claims such as exp, iss, aud, and sub, and verify signatures separately when authenticity matters.
- [What is the difference between Base64 encoding and decoding?](https://debugtools.org/answers/base64-encode-vs-decode/): Base64 encoding converts bytes or text into an ASCII-safe representation. Decoding converts that Base64 text back into the original bytes or string.
- [How can I test an API request online?](https://debugtools.org/answers/test-api-request-online/): Use an API tester to choose the method, enter the URL, add headers or auth, send the request, and inspect status, response headers, and body.
- [How do I compare two code snippets?](https://debugtools.org/answers/compare-two-code-snippets/): Paste the old snippet and new snippet into a diff tool, then review added, removed, and changed lines side by side.
- [How do I generate a hash for text?](https://debugtools.org/answers/generate-hash-for-text/): Paste text into a hash generator, choose the algorithm you need, and compare the generated digest with the expected checksum.
- [How do I decode a URL query string?](https://debugtools.org/answers/decode-url-query-string/): Use a URL decoder to convert percent-encoded characters back to readable text, then inspect each query parameter separately.
- [How do I check what an HTTP status code means?](https://debugtools.org/answers/what-http-status-code-means/): Search the status code, confirm its category, then use the meaning to decide whether the issue is client-side, server-side, redirect-related, or informational.
- [How should I use an AI debug assistant safely?](https://debugtools.org/answers/use-ai-debug-assistant-safely/): Use an AI debug assistant for non-sensitive errors, stack traces, API responses, and JSON issues, but remove secrets and private data before sending text to any configured AI provider.
- [How do I explain a stack trace?](https://debugtools.org/answers/explain-stack-trace/): Start with the exception message, then find the first frame owned by your application. That frame usually points to the code path to inspect first.
- [How do I rebuild a trace from logs?](https://debugtools.org/answers/rebuild-log-trace/): Collect logs around one failing request, group by request or trace ID, then order the events by timestamp to find the first error and downstream failures.
- [How do I analyze a HAR file?](https://debugtools.org/answers/analyze-har-file/): Load the HAR, sort by failed or slow requests, then inspect status, timing, redirects, payload size, and cache headers for the first broken dependency.
- [How do I debug a GitHub Actions failure?](https://debugtools.org/answers/debug-github-actions-failure/): Find the first failed step in the job, read a few lines above the error, then check whether the workflow command, dependency cache, secret, or environment changed.
- [How do I debug CORS and security headers?](https://debugtools.org/answers/debug-cors-security-headers/): Capture the exact response headers for the failing request, then check origin, credentials, allowed methods, CSP, cookie flags, and caching rules together.
- [How do I debug Kubernetes CrashLoopBackOff?](https://debugtools.org/answers/debug-kubernetes-crashloopbackoff/): Start with pod events and the previous container logs. CrashLoopBackOff is usually caused by process exit, failed probes, missing config, image issues, or startup dependency failures.
- [How do I inspect an OpenTelemetry trace?](https://debugtools.org/answers/inspect-opentelemetry-trace/): Find the root span, then inspect slow spans and spans with error status. The first upstream error span often explains the rest of the trace.
- [How do I fix redirect_uri_mismatch in OAuth?](https://debugtools.org/answers/debug-oauth-redirect-uri-mismatch/): Use the exact redirect_uri sent in the OAuth request and add that same scheme, host, path, and trailing slash to the provider client configuration.
- [How do I scan logs for secrets before sharing?](https://debugtools.org/answers/scan-logs-for-secrets/): Scan the log text for key, token, secret, cookie, private key, and connection-string patterns, then replace values with stable placeholders before sharing.
- [How do I generate a strong password locally?](https://debugtools.org/answers/generate-strong-password-locally/): Use a local password generator, choose a long length, include enough character variety, avoid ambiguous characters when humans must type it, and store the result in a password manager.
